prompt: What does high availability mean in the cloud?

options.text: A service can only be used by one customer
A service never changes
A service costs nothing to run
A service is designed to stay running with minimal downtime

explanation: High availability is about keeping a service running with very little downtime.

why_wrong.c: Availability is about uptime, not price.
why_wrong.a: Availability has nothing to do with exclusive use.
why_wrong.b: Services can change and still be highly available.

prompt: Which SLA allows the LEAST downtime?
explanation: The higher the percentage, the less downtime is allowed.

prompt: A retailer expects a sales spike and wants extra virtual machines added automatically, then removed afterwards. Which benefit describes this?

options.text: Elasticity
Reliability
Governance
Capital expenditure

explanation: Elasticity means resources scale automatically as demand rises and falls.

why_wrong.b: Reliability is about recovering from failures.
why_wrong.d: Capital expenditure is a type of spending, not a scaling feature.

prompt: Adding more virtual machine instances to share the load is known as what?

options.text: Scaling in
Scaling up (vertical scaling)
Failover
Scaling out (horizontal scaling)

explanation: Scaling out adds more instances to spread demand.

why_wrong.b: Scaling up makes one machine bigger.
why_wrong.c: Failover switches to a backup after a failure.

prompt: A system keeps working when one component fails and recovers automatically. Which benefit does this describe?

options.text: Elasticity
Reliability
Governance
Capital expenditure

explanation: Reliability is the ability to recover from failures and keep functioning.

why_wrong.d: Capital expenditure is a spending type.
why_wrong.c: Governance is about rules and standards.

prompt: Which TWO are examples of predictability? (Select two.)

options.text: Performance stays steady as demand changes, through autoscaling and load balancing
Tools help you forecast and track spending
You buy enough hardware for peak demand in advance
You add servers by hand whenever users complain
Every cost is fixed under a contract

explanation: Predictability covers consistent performance and forecastable cost.

why_wrong.c: Buying for peak in advance is the traditional approach, not cloud predictability.
why_wrong.d: Reacting by hand is not predictable.
why_wrong.e: Fixed contracts are not what predictability means.

prompt: Which is a governance benefit of the cloud?

options.text: Hardware is fixed and cannot be audited
Tools can enforce standards and audit resources across an environment
Compliance requirements no longer apply
The provider is responsible for all of your data security

explanation: Governance means setting rules and applying and auditing them consistently.

why_wrong.d: Customers always keep responsibility for their data.
why_wrong.c: Compliance requirements still apply in the cloud.

prompt: Using the Azure portal, command-line tools or APIs to create and manage resources is an example of what?

options.text: Capital expenditure
Elasticity
Management in the cloud (manageability)
High availability

explanation: Tools for creating and managing resources are the 'management in the cloud' side of manageability.

why_wrong.a: Capital expenditure is a spending type.

prompt: Which statement about security in the cloud is correct?

options.text: Providers offer security tools and certifications, but customers still have security responsibilities
Moving to the cloud removes all security responsibility from the customer
The cloud is always less secure than on-premises
Security tools cannot be used with cloud resources

explanation: Security in the cloud is shared: the provider secures the platform and you configure and use it correctly.

why_wrong.b: Customers always keep some responsibility, such as data and identities.
why_wrong.c: Cloud security can be strong; it depends on how it is used.
why_wrong.d: Cloud platforms provide many security tools.

prompt: Decide whether each statement about availability and scalability is true.

options.text: An SLA with a higher percentage allows less downtime.
Scaling out means adding more instances.
Elasticity means you must buy capacity in advance.

explanation: Higher SLAs mean less downtime, scaling out adds instances, and elasticity avoids paying for idle capacity in advance.

why_wrong.s3: No. Elasticity adds and removes capacity automatically.

prompt: Decide whether each statement about reliability and predictability is true.

options.text: Deploying across availability zones can improve reliability.
Predictability applies only to cost, not performance.
A reliable system can recover from failures and keep working.

explanation: Zones add redundancy, predictability covers both cost and performance, and reliability is about recovery.

why_wrong.s1: Yes. Spreading across zones adds redundancy.
why_wrong.s2: No. It covers both performance and cost.
why_wrong.s3: Yes. That is the meaning of reliability.

prompt: Decide whether each statement about manageability is true.

options.text: Automatic scaling is an example of the cloud managing resources for you.
Deploying from templates helps create consistent environments.
Manageability means you cannot use command-line tools.

explanation: Autoscaling and templates are manageability features, and command-line tools are part of managing the cloud.

why_wrong.s1: Yes. Resources adjust without manual effort.
why_wrong.s2: Yes. Templates repeat the same deployment reliably.
why_wrong.s3: No. Command-line tools are a normal way to manage resources.

prompt: Which practice supports sustainability in the cloud?

options.text: Buying enough hardware for the busiest day of the year
Scaling resources down or turning them off when demand falls
Overprovisioning in case demand rises
Leaving unused virtual machines running overnight

explanation: Matching resources to actual demand avoids waste.

why_wrong.a: Sizing for the busiest day leaves capacity idle most of the time.

prompt: A development environment is only used during business hours. What would reduce waste?

options.text: Automatically shutting it down overnight and at weekends
Keeping it running all the time
Disabling monitoring on it
Moving it to larger virtual machines

explanation: Switching off idle resources reduces unnecessary consumption.

why_wrong.d: Larger machines would use more resources.

prompt: Which TWO are sustainability-aligned practices? (Select two.)

options.text: Turn off monitoring to save effort
Monitor usage to find and remove unused resources
Leave test systems running all the time
Overprovision to avoid ever running out
Right-size resources to match demand

explanation: Right-sizing and monitoring help you use only what you need.

why_wrong.a: Monitoring is how you find waste.
